chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Mudabbir (slave with arranged emancipation) is a slave, and for his master is the right to retract regarding his emancipation; if he so desires, he sells him, and if he so desires, he gifts him, and if he so desires, he makes him a dower.

He (peace be upon him) said: And if his master leaves him upon the emancipation arrangement, and an event does not occur until his master dies, then the Mudabbir is free when his master dies, and he is from the third (of the bequest). He is at the status of a man who bequeaths with a bequest, then changes his mind for it, so he alters it before his death; and if he leaves it and does not change it until he dies, he is seized by it.

key_terms.الثُّلُث: Al-thuluth: One-third, referring to the portion of the estate allocated for bequests in Islamic inheritance law.
key_terms.الْمُدَبَّرُ: Mudabbir: A slave whose emancipation is arranged emancipation: A slave whose master has declared that he will be freed upon the master's death or at a specific time.
key_terms.تَدْبِير: Tadbir: The act of arranging emancipation for a slave.
key_terms.مَنْزِلَة: Manzilah: Status or rank, used here to compare the legal effect of tadbir to a bequest.

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for a slave with arranged emancipation (Mudabbir) if the master dies without retracting it?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the legal mechanism of 'Tadbir', where a master designates a slave for emancipation, noting that the master retains full discretion to revoke this status by selling, gifting, or using the slave as dower prior to death. If the master dies without altering the arrangement, the slave is freed, and this emancipation is treated as a bequest (Wasiyyah) deducted from one-third of the estate, mirroring the rules of a finalized will. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic view that Tadbir functions as a conditional bequest rather than an immediate transfer of ownership, ensuring it does not exceed the standard one-third limit for bequests.
